9
Two objects X and Y in an isolated system undergo a perfectly elastic collision. The velocities of
the objects before and after the collision are shown.
v
20 m s–1
12 m s–1
10 m s–1
X
Y
X
Y
before
collision
after
collision
What is the speed v of Y after the collision?
A
2.0 m s–1
B
18 m s–1
C
22 m s–1
D
24 m s–1

hints: Notice the four speeds along the same line: $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ before, $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v$ after, all to the right.
For a perfectly elastic collision, relative speed of approach before equals relative speed of separation after.
Calculate approach speed as $20 - 12$, then set $v - 10$ equal to it because Y is still ahead of X after collision.
walkthrough: Identify motion: before collision X at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is catching Y at $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$. After collision X is at $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and Y is at $v$, still ahead and to the right.
State the elastic-collision rule: along the line of impact, speed of approach = speed of separation.
Calculate approach speed before: $u_X - u_Y = 20 - 12 = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Write separation speed after: $v_Y - v_X = v - 10$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, since Y remains in front.
Equate them: $v - 10 = 8$, so $v = 18\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with correct units and same direction. This is option B.

A.explanation: Gives $v = 2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which would make Y move slower than X after collision and give the wrong relative speed of separation.

B.explanation: Gives separation speed $v - 10 = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, equal to the approach speed $20 - 12 = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ as required for a perfectly elastic collision.

C.explanation: Adds the $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ of X after collision to the approach speed instead of using $v - 10$ for separation speed along the same direction.

D.explanation: Would give separation speed $14\text{ m s}^{-1}$, larger than the $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ approach speed, which violates relative speed conservation for elastic collision.
